_comment: All values in SI units (metres, seconds, kg, radians) unless noted. Edit freely to tune balance; see knowledge.md in each package for how each constant is used.

movement._comment: v_max = base + scale*top_speed_attr ; a_max = base + scale*acceleration_attr
movement._comment_turn_speed_penalty: Max fractional reduction to the speed cap while mid-turn (0.7 = up to 70% reduction at a full 180° heading change).
movement._comment_control_speed_multiplier: Fraction of current speed retained the instant a player starts first-touch control (0.6 = 40% speed reduction on contact). The ball is immediately glued to the player and they coast at this reduced speed until control completes.

kicking._comment: sigma_angle in radians = base + scale*(1 - precision^precision_exponent). power in m/s = base + scale*attr. running_power_coefficient: max run boost = coefficient (at full sprint in line with kick). power_base/scale rescaled from 15/20 so full-sprint run_mult=1.7 gives same peak speed as old coeff=0.3 (run_mult=1.3): factor=1.3/1.7=0.765. running_direction_precision_*: reduce kick precision by up to 75% when kicking against the run direction (backwards). cos_high=0.35 (~70° forward cone), cos_low=-0.2 (~102°), penalty_mid=0.25 at cos_low, penalty_max=0.75 at cos=-1. See design doc for worked tables.

passing._comment: Auto-pace for a grounded pass: v = overshoot_factor * sqrt(2*mu_roll*g*distance), clamped to [min,max]. Error model is now unified with kicking (KickingParams) - sigma scales with both precision and effective power.
passing._comment_spinup_speed_boost: Multiplicative boost on the auto-paced launch speed (2026-09-03), compensating for ball_physics.py's ground-contact spin-up cost -- a pass launches spin-free, so it now pays a real sliding-to-rolling transition loss the original power_overshoot_factor calibration didn't account for. Linear in distance (boost = base + per_m*distance_m) since the required compensation grows with distance -- empirically fit against direct stopping-distance measurements at 10/25/40/60/65m (required boost ranged ~1.26 at 10m to ~1.57 at 65m, closely linear). See agent_plans/physics_update.md section 8. Tune further against tests/balance/test_pass_balance.py if needed; base=1.0, per_m=0.0 = no compensation.

goalkeeping._comment: 'Save' action: predicts where an incoming shot crosses the keeper's own goal line and moves the keeper there. See engine/knowledge.md for the crossing-point prediction and the ball-freeze-on-pickup rule that makes saves work with the generic possession model. early_intercept_max_distance_m: GK only attempts early interception when ball is within this range.

tackling._comment_auto_tackle: auto_tackle_overlap_factor: auto-tackle fires when player separation < factor * (r1+r2). 1.0=exact touch, 1.3=serious overlap (0.78m for standard players). auto_tackle_min_closing_mps: minimum net closing speed (carrier_speed_toward_other + other_speed_toward_carrier) to trigger.
tackling._comment_speed: tackle_attempt_tackler_speed_mult: tackler speed is immediately multiplied by this on a tackle attempt (0.6 = 40% reduction). tackle_attempt_tacklee_speed_mult: same for the tacklee (0.9 = 10% reduction). The loser additionally loses up to loser_speed_penalty_max of their speed, scaled linearly by |winner_roll - loser_roll| * loser_speed_penalty_scale, capped at loser_speed_penalty_max. 2026-09-05: retuned from (0.5, 0.8, loser_max=0.8) alongside the angle modifiers below -- eases the flat contact-speed penalty slightly while sharpening the angle-based reward/punishment, confirmed a real net win (+2-3pp win rate) for a rules-based AI that reacts to it (see orders.json's tackle_approach/jockey sections) at N=1500-3000.
tackling._comment_cooldown: tackle_cooldown_s: both tackler and tacklee enter INACTIVE_TACKLED for this duration after a tackle, preventing re-tackle spam. Players can still move and issue other orders during this time.
tackling._comment_angle: Modifier added to tackling boost based on approach angle. angle=0 (frontal, tackler is directly in front of dribbler): +15%; angle=90 (side): -10%; angle=180 (from behind): -60%. Piecewise linear in cos(angle).
tackling._comment_gk_outside: goalkeeper_outside_box_tackle_penalty: fractional reduction applied to effective_boost when a GK makes a tackle outside their own box. Reduces the 2.0 GK boost to ~1.2 — comparable to an outfield tackler, not better.
tackling._comment_control_time: control_time_penalty_reference_s: reference duration used to scale the dribbling penalty for CONTROLLING_BALL players. A player at/above this many seconds remaining gets up to 25% dribbling penalty; near 0s remaining gets no penalty.

ball_physics._comment_bounce_threshold: Min incoming vertical speed (for a ball that was actually airborne this tick, see ball_physics.py's was_grounded_before_tick gate) to count as a real bounce (apply restitution) vs. resting/rolling ground contact. Prevents a resting ball's per-tick gravity integration from being misread as a full bounce and repeatedly damping horizontal speed -- the was_grounded_before_tick gate makes this dt_s-independent by construction (fixed 2026-09-03; previously this threshold alone was only safe below dt_s ~= threshold/(gravity*bounce_restitution_vertical) =~ 0.068s, and training's sim_dt_s=0.06 was sitting at only a ~12% margin from that boundary). See engine/knowledge.md 'ground contact' note.
ball_physics._comment_bounce_friction: Replaces the old flat bounce_restitution_horizontal constant (2026-09-03). Horizontal bounce speed and spin are now derived together from a Coulomb-friction impulse at the contact point (see ball_physics.py's _resolve_bounce_friction), coupling to incident topspin/backspin/sidespin instead of applying the same fixed retention to every bounce regardless of spin. ground_friction_coefficient (mu) is the ball-on-grass friction coefficient -- used both for a bounce's instantaneous impact and (2026-09-03) for ordinary ground contact spinning a ball up toward true rolling (see _comment_ground_friction below); 0.4 sits in the main cluster of a real force-plate study of 9 actual match balls, 'The Coefficient of Friction of Soccer Balls' (measured against leather, not grass directly -- range 0.37-0.63 across balls, most clustering 0.37-0.45, e.g. Teamgeist 0.38, Kopanya 0.39, Fracas 0.41; found and checked 2026-09-03, after this value was already chosen -- it holds up, but note a grass court friction datapoint for tennis balls ran closer to ~0.6, so real grass (vs. leather) could plausibly sit higher than this). ball_inertia_shell_factor is k in I = k*m*r^2 -- a ball that fully grips (bounce or ground contact alike) retains exactly 1/(1+k) of its pre-slip horizontal speed, independent of mu. The idealized thin-pressurized-shell value is 2/3 (retention 0.6); set to 0.5 (2026-09-03, retention 0.667) as a deliberate, still-physically-defensible softening -- a real ball's panels/bladder aren't an infinitely thin shell, so a little short of the idealized 2/3 limit (but well short of 0.4 = 2/5, a solid sphere, which the ball demonstrably isn't) is a reasonable middle ground. Lowering k this way also widens the grip-vs-slide window (more bounces grip, not fewer), unlike lowering mu which would narrow it -- see agent_plans/physics_update.md.
ball_physics._comment_ground_friction: Added 2026-09-03 (see agent_plans/physics_update.md). A ball that's grounded but not yet rolling without slipping (spin doesn't match v=r*omega -- e.g. any ball launched or kicked with less spin than true rolling needs, including a plain zero-spin roll) now pays a real spin-up cost via _resolve_ground_friction, using the SAME ground_friction_coefficient/ball_inertia_shell_factor physics as a bounce, before rolling_friction_coefficient's much gentler ongoing decay takes over. This was previously unmodeled: a rolling ball's spin was never touched by ground contact at all, so 'rolling' was really 'sliding with a flat friction constant' -- physically closer to how real rolling resistance behaves, but missing the real, larger sliding-to-rolling transition cost that precedes it.

control_time._comment: Time (s) for a player to bring a ball under control on first touch. See knowledge.md in engine/ for full derivation. Jump zone (above player_height_m=1.8m): outfield_jump_scale_at_max_reach multiplies the (height_factor-1) term at outfield_max_reach_height_m; GK's height_factor_scale interpolates toward gk jump_scale_at_max_reach at gk_max_reach_height_m.
control_time._comment_control_tackle_immune: Ball height (m) above which a CONTROLLING_BALL player is immune to tackles. Default 0.95 = waist height: aerial/chest control is protected, ground control can still be challenged.

collision._comment: Player-player velocity damping on overlap. collision_velocity_retention: fraction of closing speed kept per tick (0.5 = 50% reduction). collision_damping_min_closing_speed_mps: closing speeds below this floor are left untouched, preventing unbounded compounding over many ticks of sustained overlap (see design doc for worked example).

ball_pickup._comment: Loose-ball pickup eligibility. A player within pickup_radius_m may only pick up the ball if they are CLOSING on it (relative velocity, i.e. (ball.velocity - player.velocity), has a component reducing the separation) OR the relative speed is below closing_speed_deadzone_mps (near-stationary relative motion -- e.g. a ball resting or barely rolling next to a player -- is always pickable, no need to be actively closing). This replaces the old time-based release-grace hack: a player can no longer instantly re-pick-up a ball they just kicked away at real speed, because it is moving away from them (not closing) -- with no special-casing of 'who kicked it'. It also naturally lets a ball rolling past a slow/stationary player be picked up only if the player has a real closing velocity component toward it, not by proximity alone. See engine/knowledge.md.
ball_pickup._comment_armed_redirect_settle_vz: Match._update_loose_ball_pickup's armed-redirect gate: an armed push-kick redirect is only honoured while the ball's vertical speed is at or below this. Originally 1e-6 (effectively 'exactly zero') to stop a redirect firing on genuinely wrong mid-bounce data -- but a push-kick's own kick-angle noise routinely gives it some small vz (commonly ~0.5-0.6 m/s), so 1e-6 almost never re-settles before a fast-sprinting player recatches it, forcing every touch through the slow CONTROLLING_BALL grant instead (defeating the point of arming at all -- confirmed via a real traced episode: 40 short, speed-losing hops instead of ~7 long full-speed ones). Tuned empirically across 500 real episodes at 0.01/0.5/0.7/1.0/1.5: timeouts fell monotonically from 7/502 to 3/502 as this loosened, flattening out by 1.0 (1.0 and 1.5 were identical); 0.5 was a notably bad in-between choice since it sits right on ball_physics.rolling_friction/bounce_threshold_mps (also 0.5), making the redirect decision flip on the same noise that decides real-bounce-vs-settle. 1.0 is comfortably clear of that boundary with all the measured benefit.
